scope: argv-and-environment forwarding contract of the installed opencode wrapper, proven with a stand-in recorder executable

method.seam: APPDATA is redirected at the batch level to a private temp tree whose npm\node_modules\opencode-ai\bin\opencode.exe is the recorder. That is step 1 of the helper's own Resolve-RealOpencode, so the INSTALLED opencode.cmd and omo-opencode-port.ps1 were executed completely unmodified and resolved the recorder with no production edit and no backdoor.
method.recorder: a C# ConsoleApplication compiled in-place with Add-Type -OutputAssembly; it writes its complete argv, its OPENCODE_PORT, its TMUX and its own image path to $OMO_RECORDER_OUT as UTF-8 and exits 0 immediately.
method.why_no_console_capture: every case asserts against the recorder's own UTF-8 file, not against a pipe, because ProcessStartInfo+ReadToEndAsync is unreliable on this host. The wrapper's own stdout was still redirected to a file and measured, and is reported per case.
method.encoding: recorder output written with UTF8Encoding(false) and read back with ReadAllBytes + explicit UTF-8 decode. The driver's console is CP950/Big5, which is separately demonstrated in case c9.
method.timeouts: 25 s per case; zero cases timed out, so no wrapper/child teardown was needed
method.teardown_order: wrapper (powershell) then cmd root, implemented but unused because nothing hung

suspected_defects.severity: minor / parity-faithful but wrong in practice
suspected_defects.observed: argv==["--port","0"] and OPENCODE_PORT=0 forwarded verbatim, no bind attempted, exit 0.
suspected_defects.expected_by_this_task: fall back to a bind and yield a port in 7801-7901.
suspected_defects.analysis: The helper mirrors /home/daniel/.bashrc:61-63, whose case "$port" in ""|*[!0-9]*) accepts "0" as valid, so the helper is a faithful port. But port 0 is not a bindable target: the Linux reference would then run opencode --port 0, and OmO resolveServerUrl reads env.OPENCODE_PORT verbatim rather than re-validating it. The plan text (todo 7) and the bash reference disagree with each other here; the wrapper follows the bash reference. NOT FIXED - reported only, per instructions.
suspected_defects.secondary_note: the same gap exists in /home/daniel/.bashrc, so fixing only the Windows side would create a divergence.

c1_tmux_unset_passthrough.assertion: TMUX unset: argv must be byte-identical, no --port, no port logic
c1_tmux_unset_passthrough.why: argv byte-identical to the three tokens sent; no --port prepended; OPENCODE_PORT absent from child env

c2_tmux_set_no_args.assertion: TMUX set, no args: argv == ["--port", n], OPENCODE_PORT == n in 7801-7901

c2b_busy_7801_7802.assertion: 7801+7802 held busy: real bind probe must skip them and pick 7803
c2b_busy_7801_7802.why: argv==["--port","7803"] with OPENCODE_PORT=7803; p in 7801-7901; 7801 and 7802 were HELD BOUND by the driver, so reaching 7803 proves a real exclusive bind probe, not a liveness check or a fixed default

c3_tmux_set_port_1234.why: argv forwarded unchanged as two tokens; no auto-bind; OPENCODE_PORT absent

c4a_ocp_8199_held_busy.assertion: OPENCODE_PORT=8199 while 8199 is HELD BOUND: proves env trusted, no bind attempted
c4a_ocp_8199_held_busy.why: OPENCODE_PORT=8199 used verbatim WHILE the driver held an exclusive listener on 8199; a bind of 8199 would have failed, so the fact that it did not touch the socket proves the env value short-circuits the probe entirely

c4b_ocp_8123_no_listener.assertion: OPENCODE_PORT=8123 with nothing bound: a real bind probe would have returned 7801, so 8123 proves no bind
c4b_ocp_8123_no_listener.why: OPENCODE_PORT=8123 with 7801 free; a probe would have returned 7801, obtaining 8123 proves no bind occurred

c5a_ocp_nonnumeric.assertion: OPENCODE_PORT=abc must fall back to a bind
c5a_ocp_nonnumeric.why: OPENCODE_PORT=abc rejected as non-integer; fell back to a bind and got 7801 (in range)

c5b_ocp_zero.assertion: OPENCODE_PORT=0 - task expects fallback; bash reference accepts 0
c5b_ocp_zero.why: OPENCODE_PORT=0 was ACCEPTED as a valid integer: argv==["--port", "0"] OPENCODE_PORT='0', no bind, port 0 forwarded verbatim. The task expects a fallback to a real bind. /home/daniel/.bashrc:61-63 accepts "0" identically (case ""|*[!0-9]*) so this is faithful parity, but "port 0" is not a usable bind target and OmO resolveServerUrl would read it verbatim.

c9_non_ascii_arg_informational.assertion: informational only: non-ASCII argv token; records the .cmd bytes and the recorder bytes so the mangling layer can be attributed
c9_non_ascii_arg_informational.why: non-ASCII argv token mangled, but by cmd.exe and NOT by the wrapper: the .cmd bytes on disk are the correct UTF-8 636166c3a92de4b8ade69687, the recorder received caf<U+77C7>-<U+927D><U+525C>? which is the Big5/CP950 reading of those same bytes. This is the documented console-encoding hazard on this host, upstream of opencode.cmd. Any wrapper-level byte-identity claim is unaffected: the tokens the wrapper received are echoed back unchanged.
